College placement cells in India often paint an exaggerated picture to attract new admissions. They advertise high average salary packages based on a handful of top placements, while the majority of students get offers with low pay or none at all. Many colleges count unpaid internships or irrelevant job roles as “placements” to inflate statistics.

In some cases, mass recruiters hiring for low-skill roles are showcased as major success stories. There’s also pressure on students to accept any offer just to boost the college’s numbers. These misleading practices create false hope and mask the real gap between education and employability.
